scope: Controlled diagnostic sample for parent-sheet size, watermark/stock time, cutting-format and work-operation hypotheses in Hodgson-associated paper objects. This is not a complete collection census.
central_claim: Repeated working formats can persist across heterogeneous paper stocks. Object dimensions therefore need to be modelled as the result of parent-sheet manufacture plus post-procurement cutting/folding/trimming, not as a direct proxy for stock identity or maker.

standard_size_reference.source: British Association of Paper Historians, Old English Paper Sizes

source_control_rules: Dimensional match alone does not prove parent-sheet size.
No catalogue watermark statement does not mean no watermark is present.
Watermark date, maker, commercial size, working format and use date are independent fields.
Do not turn visible watermark counts into stock percentages.
Do not infer task/support determinism from small cross-collection samples.
Keep working paper dimensions separate from later mount/frame dimensions.
Physical edge, formation and transmitted-light evidence outrank dimensional reconstruction.
